The Apostle's primary armament is a single Sniper artillery piece mounted in the hull, supported by three tons of ammunition providing thirty rounds of sustained fire. An advanced fire control system guides the weapon, enabling accurate engagement of targets at extreme range, while the ammunition capacity permits the crew to carry multiple munition types as the tactical situation demands. A single front-mounted small laser provides minimal self-defense capability against threats that manage to reach the gun line.

Powered by an internal combustion engine, the Apostle achieves a cruise speed of thirty-two kilometers per hour with a flank speed of fifty-four. Its generous fuel supply provides an operational range of nearly eleven hundred kilometers, well suited to extended campaigns. Five tons of BAR 6 armor afford basic protection, reflecting the expectation that the vehicle would operate well behind the front lines rather than engage in direct combat. A tractor chassis modification allows the Apostle to tow additional equipment or ammunition trailers, extending its logistical footprint. The large crew of ten, including two officers and six dedicated gunners, ensures smooth operation of the complex artillery system.

The Apostle is an eighty-ton primitive self-propelled artillery vehicle commissioned by the Terran Hegemony in 2321. Designed alongside its lighter companion, the Reaper, the Apostle represented the heavier of two artillery platforms developed to modernize the Hegemony Armed Forces' outdated indirect fire capabilities. Intended to provide long-range heavy fire support at the division level, the vehicle was assigned to battalion-sized artillery formations supporting HAF divisions in the field. As one of the earliest purpose-built self-propelled guns fielded by the Hegemony, the Apostle established a new standard for mobile artillery support that would influence Hegemony military doctrine for generations to come.

The Apostle Self-Propelled Artillery served as the primary heavy indirect fire platform for Hegemony Armed Forces division-level operations. Its substantial ammunition capacity and long operational range made it well suited to sustained bombardment campaigns in support of frontline formations. The tractor chassis allowed Apostle batteries to tow additional supplies during extended operations, making the vehicle the centerpiece of HAF heavy artillery battalions.

The Apostle and Reaper emerged from a period of urgent military reform following James McKenna's rise to power as the first Director-General of the Terran Hegemony. Field Marshal Mears Coblitz, retained as Commanding General, recognized that the fractured remnants of the old Terran Alliance military desperately needed modernization to prevent the Hegemony from descending into civil war. Among his priorities, the artillery corps had long suffered from neglect, relying on outdated static, towed, and self-propelled pieces inherited from the Alliance era.

Coblitz personally drafted requirements for two new self-propelled artillery vehicles. The Apostle filled the heavier role, intended for assignment to division-level artillery battalions, while the Reaper served a lighter requirement at the regimental and brigade level. Both vehicles entered service remarkably quickly, debuting in less than two years from initial requirements. The Apostle first saw combat during the later stages of the Campaign of Persuasion, as the Hegemony worked to expand and strengthen its influence across nearby star systems.

Throughout the late twenty-third century and the decades that followed, the Apostle and Reaper gradually supplanted virtually all of the older Alliance artillery still in service. Both platforms remained in frontline use for more than a century before advancing technology rendered them obsolete. The Apostle received its formal obsolescence designation in 2485, replaced by newer designs incorporating standard rather than primitive technology. Despite this, a handful of examples survived into the thirty-first century. By the dawn of the Dark Age, at least a few Apostles remained as ceremonial vehicles stationed on Terra and New Earth.

The Reaper centers its firepower on a single Thumper artillery piece, complemented by three tons of ammunition providing sixty rounds of fire. An advanced fire control system with anti-aircraft targeting capability guides the weapon, giving the Reaper a secondary role as an impromptu air defense battery when circumstances demand. A front-mounted small laser serves as the vehicle's sole direct-fire defensive weapon.

The Reaper's internal combustion engine propels it at a cruise speed of thirty-two kilometers per hour with a flank speed of fifty-four, matching the Apostle in ground mobility. However, its single ton of fuel limits operational range to approximately 526 kilometers, considerably less than its heavier companion. Protection consists of 3.5 tons of BAR 6 armor, providing minimal coverage against anything beyond small arms and shrapnel. The vehicle suffers from poor environmental sealing, leaving the seven-member crew vulnerable to chemical, biological, or hazardous atmosphere conditions. Despite these limitations, the Reaper's lighter weight made it more practical for wider distribution across the HAF's regimental structure than the larger and more resource-intensive Apostle.

The Reaper is a fifty-five-ton primitive self-propelled artillery vehicle introduced by the Terran Hegemony in 2321. Developed as the lighter counterpart to the heavier Apostle, the Reaper was designed to provide indirect fire support at the regimental and brigade level, filling a critical gap in the Hegemony Armed Forces' artillery capabilities. More mobile and numerous than its larger sibling, the Reaper traded raw firepower for flexibility and wider tactical deployment across the HAF's organizational structure. As one of the first generation of purpose-built Hegemony artillery platforms, the Reaper helped establish the doctrinal foundations for mobile fire support at the formation level.

The Reaper Self-Propelled Artillery served as the standard light artillery platform for Hegemony Armed Forces regiment and brigade-level formations. Its lighter weight and simpler logistics allowed wider distribution than its heavier companion, providing responsive indirect fire support closer to the front lines. The advanced fire control system's anti-aircraft targeting capability gave Reaper crews an additional air defense role, making the vehicle a versatile addition to formation-level artillery battalions.

The Reaper originated alongside the Apostle as part of Field Marshal Mears Coblitz's comprehensive modernization of the Hegemony Armed Forces' artillery arm during the early years of the Terran Hegemony. While the Apostle addressed the need for heavy fire support at the division level, the Reaper filled the lighter requirement for regimental and brigade artillery battalions. Both vehicles moved from requirements to production remarkably fast, entering service in less than two years.

The Reaper's first operational deployment came during the later stages of the Campaign of Persuasion, where the HAF's newly modernized artillery corps proved its worth in supporting ground actions across multiple worlds. The lighter vehicle was particularly valued for its ability to be distributed more widely across the HAF's expanding force structure, providing organic fire support to formations that had previously relied on outdated Alliance-era equipment.

Over the following decades, the Reaper and Apostle together displaced virtually all of the static, towed, and self-propelled artillery that the Hegemony had inherited from the Terran Alliance. Both platforms served for more than a century before the rapid pace of technological advancement overtook them. The Reaper was declared obsolete in 2480, slightly earlier than the Apostle, as newer designs employing what would become standard technology in later eras entered production. Few Reapers survived beyond their period of active service. By the thirty-first century, the remaining examples had been relegated to purely ceremonial roles, with a handful of relics enduring into the Dark Age as static displays on Terra and New Earth.
